Marta G.: Heads-up — Veridian sent their security questionnaire this morning. ~60 items but they highlighted RBAC, audit logging retention, KMS key management, vuln triage, and incident response SLAs. Can we triage answers quickly?
Samir K.: Ack. I can take RBAC + audit logging. Do we have a baseline for retention policies to cite?
Jordan S.: I can own KMS + key rotation questions. Lia, can you handle SOC2/SLA phrasing and IR process?
Lia R.: Yes — will draft SOC2 evidence references and IR timeline. Quick Q: Veridian asked if we support per-tenant key isolation. We do via Dedicated/Private, right?
Jordan S.: Correct — for Private and Dedicated we can integrate customer-supplied keys (KMS/HSM) and support per-tenant CMKs. For hosted we offer customer-managed KMS for Enterprise plans.
Marta G.: Samir — for RBAC they want a matrix: role names, permissions, provisioning flow, and recent changes. Use our current mapping but call out that we support SCIM provisioning + SSO groups.
Samir K.: Will do. Also they asked for audit log ingestion format and retention. We retain admin/auth events for 13 months by default and operational API logs for 90 days in hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention longer. Draft snippet:
```yaml
audit:
  retention_default: 90d
  admin_retention: 395d
  formats: [json, syslog]
  export: s3://<bucket> or push-to-splunk
```
Jordan S.: That looks good. Add that logs include actor, action, resource, request_id, and model_version. Also mention immutable append-only storage for exported logs.
Lia R.: IR playbook — they want mean time to acknowledge/escalate. Our SLO is 15 min ack for P0 incidents, 1 hour for P1. We also offer dedicated oncall for enterprise with 24/7 rotation. I'll add the escalation diagram.
Marta G.: Vulnerability triage question: they want our process for external CVE notices and patch timelines. Samir, do we have standard SLA?
Samir K.: We triage within 24h of public disclosure, assign severity using CVSS + business impact, and target mitigations within 7 days for critical infra vulns; model/security regressions follow a separate rollback + mitigation cadence (usually 48–72h). Will note exception windows for vendor dependencies.
Jordan S.: For KMS Qs — they asked about key rotation and access audit. We rotate service keys annually by default and support customer rotation schedules. Access to keys is audited in Cloud KMS logs; we can provide access logs tied to request_ids.
Marta G.: They also asked whether we store plaintext customer data in logs. Answer: we redact PII/token payloads by default from platform logs; customers can enable full payload capture for debugging under NDA.
Lia R.: I'm adding language around encryption: in-transit TLS1.2+ and at-rest AES-256. Add link to our crypto whitepaper in the response.
Samir K.: One more: RBAC change history. We can provide admin audit for role grants and service-principal changes (CSV export). I'll include a redacted sample.
Marta G.: Cool. Action items: Samir — RBAC matrix + audit retention sample; Jordan — KMS key isolation + rotation + logs; Lia — SOC2 + IR timeline + encryption language. I'll assemble into the questionnaire doc and write the cover email.
Jordan S.: FYI adding a short config example for customer-managed KMS integration:
```json
{
  "kms_provider":"gcp-kms",
  "key_path":"projects/abc/locations/global/keyRings/v1/cryptoKeys/veridian-key",
  "access_audit_enabled":true
}
```
